stem: Which of the following statements are true about Akashteer?

options.label: a
options.text: Akashteer is the core of the Indian Army’s air defence system.

options.label: b
options.text: It integrates seamlessly with India’s wider C4ISR system.

options.label: c
options.text: It reflects a strategic shift from passive defence to active and rapid counter-action.

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Akashteer is the main command-and-control system of the Army’s air defence setup, through which different air defence units, radars, and weapon systems are connected as a network. It functions in integration with India’s larger C4ISR (Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance) ecosystem and enables coordinated working among the three services. It automatically monitors the low-altitude airspace and efficiently controls ground-based air defence weapon systems, thereby shifting India’s strategy from passive defence to active and rapid counter-action. Therefore, option (d) is correct.

stem: A sudden rise in the barometric height indicates

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: A barometer is an instrument that measures atmospheric pressure and helps in weather forecasting. A sudden rise in the barometer reading indicates extremely dry weather, whereas a sudden fall indicates stormy conditions. A gradual fall in the barometer reading suggests the possibility of rainfall.

stem: Quartz crystals used in clocks are :

expl: Quartz crystals used in watches are silicon dioxide (SiO). In nature, some forms are found as rock crystal and rhinestone. However, those used commercially are generally man-made. Quartz crystals are also used in radio and television.

stem: Which of the following is the value of the solar constant ?
expl: The solar constant is the amount of solar energy received per second per unit area at the upper boundary of the Earth’s atmosphere. It is also defined as the flux density of solar radiation. It is not a truly constant value, because it can vary with time. According to NASA, the solar constant is about 1.361 kW/m², and it keeps varying between 1.360 and 1.367 kW/m². Therefore, the nearest option (b) is correct.

stem: Which of the following is a non-contact force ?
expl: Magnetic force is an example of a non-contact force, whereas frictional force and impact force are examples of contact forces. In non-contact forces, objects are unlikely to come into direct contact with each other.

stem: In 2012, a highly publicized 'God particle' was discovered at the CERN European Laboratory. The scientific name of this particle is:
expl: In 2012, through experiments at the Large Hadron Collider in the CERN European Laboratory, the ‘Higgs boson’, popularly called the ‘God particle’, was discovered. This hypothesis was presented in 1964 by Nobel Prize–winning scientist Peter Higgs. The particle was named the Higgs boson after Higgs and the Indian scientist Satyendra Nath Bose.

stem: Which of the following photoelectric devices is most suitable for digital applications?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: A photovoltaic cell is generally called a solar cell. It is a non-mechanical device that converts sunlight directly into electricity, whereas a photodiode is a detector of light signals. Therefore, for digital applications (switching/controlling), a photodiode is used. It is notable that solar light is made up of photons. These photons contain different amounts of energy corresponding to different wavelengths of the solar spectrum. Photovoltaic cells are made of semiconductor materials. When photons strike these cells, they transfer energy to them. A photo-emissive device converts electrical energy into light energy, such as LEDs and other light emitters.

stem: The credit for research and development in space science goes to—
expl: In India, the main source of inspiration for research and development in space science was the renowned space scientist Dr. Vikram Sarabhai. Dr. V. Sarabhai was the first Chairman of the Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR), formed in 1962. In place of INCOSPAR, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was formed in 1969.

stem: The father of the Indian program in atomic energy is—
expl: Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha is the father of the Indian atomic energy program. In India, on 10 August 1948, the Atomic Energy Commission was constituted under the chairmanship of Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha.

stem: In using nuclear power for peaceful purposes, India is far ahead of which country?
expl: Pakistan, which conducted nuclear tests following India's nuclear tests. However, Pakistan’s nuclear program is focused on developing nuclear weapons, whereas the main objective of India’s nuclear program is its peaceful use through nuclear power generation. India passed the Atomic Energy Act in 1948 and clearly declared that nuclear research would be used for peaceful progress. In terms of nuclear power generation and other nuclear applications that improve human life (such as medical uses, food preservation, etc.), India is far ahead of Pakistan.

stem: The name of the tank manufactured in India is—
expl: Among the given options, the tank manufactured in India is Arjun. It was developed for the Indian Army by the Combat Vehicles Research and Development Establishment (CVRDE) of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO). It is a third-generation main battle tank.

stem: When was the first Indian satellite Aryabhata launched?
expl: India’s first satellite ‘Aryabhata’ was launched on 19 April 1975 from Kapustin Yar using the Soviet Kosmos-3M rocket. The satellite was named after the ancient Indian mathematician Aryabhata.
